niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces that feel polished, intentional, and clearly structured, with strong hierarchy, visible actionability, and enough content to feel complete rather than empty. They often respond well to bold contrast, prominent CTAs, modular card/list organization, and contemporary premium styling, but this varies by context: in onboarding/privacy flows they also repeatedly favor calmer, lighter, more spacious, less promotional presentations. Overall, they like interfaces that are easy to scan, visually decisive, and purpose-built rather than generic or placeholder-like.

criteria.description: Prefers screens that look fully realized, populated, and functional rather than sparse, placeholder-like, partial, or unfinished.
Prefers strong, obvious hierarchy with clear progression between title, sections, controls, and content blocks.
Prefers interfaces where primary and secondary actions are immediately visible, clearly labeled, and easy to understand.
Prefers content arranged for quick scanning, with rows/cards that expose useful information at a glance.
Prefers fewer competing focal points, less clutter, and cleaner presentation over noisy or overly busy compositions.
Prefers clearly segmented sections or modules with consistent organization rather than mixed or weakly grouped content.
Prefers interfaces that feel curated, modern, and intentionally styled rather than template-like, generic, or dated.
Prefers enough visible information and options to feel useful and complete, but not so many competing elements that the screen feels crowded.
Prefers well-defined UI components with readable boundaries and distinct modules rather than weakly separated blended elements.
Prefers a strong, obvious primary call to action that anchors the screen and signals what to do next.
Prefers layouts that use the canvas purposefully, avoiding large dead zones, top-heavy emptiness, or wasted space.
Prefers repeating, orderly row/card treatments that create steady rhythm and predictable scanning.
Prefers search bars and controls that feel integrated into the page rather than detached, stark, or mechanically inserted.
Prefers stronger text presence and legible labeling that helps sections and actions stand out clearly.
Prefers interfaces that foreground practical task completion and operational clarity over decorative or purely promotional framing.
When sections are separated, prefers gentler dividers, softer containers, or subtle framing over harsh compartmentalization.
Prefers visible identity or personality cues such as avatars, photos, or distinctive item markers when they improve recognition and scanability.
